name: The Iron Corridor

stars.name: Gauntlet Prime
stars.notes: Primary star of a wide binary. Its habitable zone supports three inhabited worlds—a rarity that makes this system one of the most strategically valuable chokepoints in the sector.

stars.name: Gauntlet Secundus
stars.notes: Dim red dwarf companion orbiting at approximately 200 AU. Its single rocky planet serves as a remote listening post. The star's faintness makes the outer system an ideal staging area for covert fleet movements.

planets.name: Sentry
planets.notes: Inner rocky world bristling with automated weapons platforms and sensor arrays. Serves as the first layer of system defense, capable of engaging hostile vessels before they reach the inhabited zone.

planets.name: Portcullis
planets.notes: Arid but habitable world controlling the inner approach to the corridor. Home to 3.8 million, primarily military families and support industries. The surface is dominated by fortress-cities with integrated anti-orbital defenses.

planets.name: Corridor Prime
planets.notes: The system's jewel—a water-rich world with 12 million inhabitants. The largest population center and economic hub, though its economy is entirely war-driven. Shipyards in orbit produce warships at an industrial pace.

planets.name: Rearguard
planets.notes: Cool, mountainous world with 2.1 million inhabitants. Serves as the system's fallback position—deep bunker complexes in the mountains house command-and-control infrastructure designed to survive orbital bombardment.

planets.name: Arsenal
planets.notes: Airless world converted into the largest ammunition depot in the sector. Underground magazines stretch for kilometers. Three moons host additional weapons storage and fleet maintenance facilities.

planets.name: Rampart
planets.notes: Massive gas giant whose extensive moon system hosts fleet anchorages, fuel processing, and the sector's primary naval academy. It is the keystone of the system's outer defenses.

planets.name: Glacis
planets.notes: Frozen outer world with deep-range sensor installations monitoring the approaches from neighboring systems. Unmanned kill-sats orbit in dense constellations.

planets.name: Far Picket
planets.notes: Remote rocky body orbiting the M3V companion star. Houses a covert listening post and emergency fleet rally point. Its existence is classified.

anomalies.name: The Gauntlet
anomalies.notes: The overlapping gravity wells of three inhabited worlds create a navigational channel that any fleet must traverse to pass through the system. This natural chokepoint is why the Iron Corridor is worth fighting over—whoever holds it controls transit across the entire Gauntlet Reach sector.

anomalies.name: Ghost Fleet
anomalies.notes: A formation of 34 derelict warships from the Battle of the Corridor (2698), left in their final positions as a memorial. Their running lights were reactivated and they drift in perpetual formation, a fleet of the dead.

asteroid_belts.name: Foundry Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Extraordinarily rich metallic belt that supplies the Corridor Prime shipyards with raw materials. Mining operations run continuously under military escort. Control of this belt alone justifies the system's strategic value.

stations.name: Corridor Command
stations.notes: Sector fleet headquarters and the largest military installation in the Gauntlet Reach. A city-sized station housing strategic command, fleet operations, intelligence, and logistics coordination for the entire theater.

stations.name: Portcullis Gate
stations.notes: Forward defense station controlling the inner approach. Equipped with heavy anti-ship batteries and fighter squadrons. Designed to delay an attacking fleet long enough for the main battle group to deploy.

stations.name: Keel Yard
stations.notes: Primary warship construction facility. Currently producing destroyers and cruisers at a rate of one hull every six weeks. The yard operates around the clock and has not paused production in eleven years.

stations.name: The Exchange
stations.location: Lagrange point between Corridor Prime and Rearguard
stations.notes: Despite the military nature of the system, enormous volumes of materiel flow through the Corridor. The Exchange handles procurement, contract negotiation, and the gray-market trade that lubricates any war economy.

faction_control.primary: Contested — Terran Gauntlet Command / Vreth Imperium
faction_control.notes: The Iron Corridor is the single most strategically important system in the Gauntlet Reach—whoever controls it controls transit across the sector. Terran Gauntlet Command currently holds the system but faces persistent Vreth Imperium probing attacks, sabotage operations, and the constant threat of a full-scale assault. Three major battles have been fought for this system; a fourth is considered inevitable.

history: The Iron Corridor's strategic significance was recognized immediately upon its discovery in 2487. Its three habitable worlds, rich asteroid belt, and natural navigational chokepoint made it the key to controlling the entire Gauntlet Reach sector. Colonization was military-led from the start.

The Battle of the Corridor in 2698 was the system's defining moment: a Vreth Imperium assault fleet of 200+ warships attempted to force the chokepoint. The defense held, but at the cost of 34 Terran warships and 19,000 lives. The Ghost Fleet memorial marks where the line held.

Since 2698, the system has been in a state of permanent military readiness. The Keel Yard has not stopped building warships. The fortifications grow deeper every year. Intelligence reports indicate the Vreth Imperium is massing for another attempt. The question is not whether the next battle will come, but when—and whether the Corridor will hold a second time.
description: The Iron Corridor is a system that exists to be defended. Eight worlds orbit a yellow star and its dim red companion, three of them inhabited, all of them militarized. The natural chokepoint created by overlapping gravity wells between orbits two and four means any fleet transiting the Gauntlet Reach sector must pass through this system—and through the layered defenses that Terran Gauntlet Command has spent decades building. From the automated weapons platforms on Sentry to the deep bunkers of Rearguard, every element of this system is oriented toward a single purpose: holding the line.

The economy of the Iron Corridor is the economy of war. Corridor Prime's shipyards produce warships continuously. The Foundry Belt feeds them raw materials. Arsenal stores enough ammunition to fight a campaign measured in years. Eighteen million people live in this system, and virtually every one of them works in support of the military mission—building ships, maintaining defenses, training soldiers, or processing the materiel that flows through the Exchange. Civilian life exists, but it exists in the shadow of the fortress.

The Iron Corridor's strategic value makes it a magnet for every kind of operator. Military contractors find unlimited work. Arms dealers supply the insatiable demand for weapons and ammunition. Intelligence operatives from half a dozen factions probe the system's defenses and counter-probe each other. The Exchange handles billions in procurement contracts, and where there are contracts, there is corruption. And always, in the background, the knowledge that the Vreth Imperium is building toward another assault—one that may be larger, better planned, and harder to stop than the last.
